title: Event
description: Envelope for every event published to the NATS subject tree events.>. A CloudEvents 1.0 event in structured JSON mode, with a stricter profile: time, subject and dataversion are required, and source, subject and type are restricted to NATS-safe tokens so they can form the subject events.<source>.<subject>.<type>. See docs/events.md.

id.description: Globally unique event identifier and idempotency key. Content-derived hash when the event has a natural identity, so a retried publish deduplicates; otherwise a UUIDv7. Also sent as the Nats-Msg-Id header so JetStream drops duplicates inside its window.

source.description: The component that published the event, e.g. heimdall, urd, eir. Equals the second subject token, and the publisher's NATS user may publish only under events.<source>.>, so the value is enforced by the broker.

subject.description: The service the event is about. Equal to source when a service reports on itself; different when a collector reports on something else, e.g. source heimdall, subject exo.

type.description: What happened, as dotted lower-case segments ending in a past-tense verb: request.served, status.changed, metric.observed. Each segment becomes a subject token.

time.description: When the event happened (not when it was published), RFC 3339 in UTC with an upper-case T and Z, millisecond precision.

dataversion.description: Version of the data payload's shape for this type. Starts at 1; bump on any change a consumer could notice. A CloudEvents extension attribute.

correlationid.description: Optional. Joins related events across services, e.g. an agent session id or an upstream request id. A CloudEvents extension attribute.

host.description: Optional. The machine the event was produced on, by its short role name. A CloudEvents extension attribute.

data.description: The payload: metadata only, never prompt or response bodies or secrets. Shape is defined per (type, dataversion) in docs/events.md. Keys are snake_case; quantities carry their unit as a suffix (_ms, _bytes, _pct).
